patterns.label: A person appears for the first time
patterns.when: a named person is introduced (born, rose to power, 'a man named', first mention of a key figure)

slots.role: label under the name, max 28 chars (e.g. 'FIRST PRESIDENT')

sequence: Establish the place with a wide background and a place+year banner.
The person walks or pops in, big, in their signature outfit.
A name card appears with a role label (this is the only time the label is needed).
One prop that sums them up sits beside them (quill, sword, lightbulb).
They do one characteristic action while a short in-character line bubbles up.
Supporting people react or stand smaller behind.
patterns.camera: Start wide, push in slowly on the person while the name card appears.
patterns.timing: name card on the word that says the name; role label +0.4 s; line on the key verb.
patterns.background: the place where they were at that moment
examples: George Washington became the first president.
patterns.source: seed: documented technique, not yet frame-verified

patterns.label: A head of state or commander appears
patterns.when: a king, president, emperor, general or dictator takes the stage (role words: president, king, emperor, general, tsar, chancellor)
sequence: Wide establishing shot of the seat of power (palace, hall, capitol).
Leader steps up to the center, larger than anyone else, with the crown/hat that marks the role.
A flag or banner of their side unfolds behind them.
Name card + title.
Advisors or soldiers stand smaller on both sides; one reacts.
patterns.camera: Slow zoom 1.0 to 1.08 on the leader; hold.
patterns.timing: name card on the name word; flag on the country word.
patterns.background: palace or interior or field with banners
examples: Napoleon crowned himself emperor.
Stalin took over the Soviet Union.
patterns.source: seed: documented technique, not yet frame-verified

patterns.label: Someone gives a speech to a crowd
patterns.when: a speech, address, rally, announcement or broadcast to a crowd or to the nation

slots.sign: a banner text behind the speaker (optional)

sequence: Wide: speaker small at the podium, crowd below, banners.
Cut to a close-up of the speaker on the key phrase.
Quote appears as a speech bubble or big text.
Crowd reacts (cheer, boo, silence) on the next clause.
Pull back out to show the size of the crowd.
patterns.camera: Close-up on the speaker exactly on the punchline word; whip or pull back to the crowd after.
patterns.timing: quote on the word before it is spoken; crowd reaction 0.4 s after.
patterns.characters: speaker scale 1.1 at a podium, crowd 10-24 smaller
patterns.background: field, street, palace balcony or hall
examples: Hitler promised the crowd jobs and revenge.
Lincoln gave a short speech at Gettysburg.
patterns.source: seed: documented technique, not yet frame-verified

patterns.label: A document is signed
patterns.when: a treaty, law, constitution or declaration is signed or sealed

slots.doc_title: the document's real name, uppercase, max 22 chars
slots.doc_lines: 2-4 short lines actually written on it

sequence: Establish the room.
The document slides to the center and grows large enough to read, title first.
The signer picks up the quill; witnesses stand around and watch.
Close-up on the pen touching the paper on the word 'signed'.
A stamp or seal lands; witnesses react.
Cut to what the signature changed (next beat).
patterns.camera: Push in on the document; close-up on the pen at the verb.
patterns.timing: document on its name; pen on 'signed'; stamp +0.8 s.
patterns.characters: signer scale 1.0 on the left, 1-3 witnesses smaller on the right
patterns.actions: signer: write/nod; witnesses: cheer or gasp
patterns.props: document or scroll (with title and lines), quill, table
examples: The Treaty of Versailles was signed in 1919.
Jefferson wrote the Declaration of Independence.
patterns.source: seed: documented technique, not yet frame-verified

patterns.label: A law is debated and passed
patterns.when: a legislature votes: congress, parliament, a senate or a convention passes a law, bill or amendment

slots.doc_lines: 2-3 short lines of what it says
slots.speaker: who speaks (optional)

sequence: Establish the chamber (benches, flags, columns) and the place+year banner.
Representatives debate: one stands and speaks, others react.
The document appears, big, with its real title.
A vote counter ticks up: YES vs NO.
Result stamp (PASSED / REJECTED) and the room reacts.
Transition into the consequences.
patterns.camera: Wide first, then slow push toward the speaker; close-up on the counter at the result.
patterns.timing: document on its name; counter during the verb 'voted'; stamp on the result word.
patterns.characters: speaker at the front, 8-16 delegates in two blocks
examples: Congress passed the Stamp Act in 1765.
Parliament voted to end the slave trade.
patterns.source: seed: documented technique, not yet frame-verified

patterns.label: Two sides argue
patterns.when: two people or parties argue, disagree or split into factions

slots.issue: what they argue about (a prop or sign)

sequence: Two podiums or two groups face each other, the issue symbol (document, coin, flag) between them.
Left side speaks: bubble.
Camera whips to the right side: reply bubble.
Third beat: crowd between them looks left and right.
End on one side steaming (vein, steam) and the other smug.
patterns.camera: Whip between the two sides on each line.
patterns.timing: left line on the first verb, right line 1.2 s later.
patterns.characters: two leaders facing each other scale 1.1, a few followers each
patterns.props: issue prop in the middle, podiums
examples: Hamilton wanted a strong bank, Jefferson hated the idea.
patterns.source: seed: documented technique, not yet frame-verified

patterns.label: Voting and a result
patterns.when: an election, campaign, voting or a landslide
sequence: People queue at a ballot box on a street.
Candidates wave on stages left and right.
A tally counter runs.
Winner is lifted; loser slumps.
Result banner.
patterns.camera: Slow pan across the queue, zoom on the counter.
patterns.timing: counter on 'votes'/'percent'; winner pose on the result verb.
examples: Lincoln won the 1860 election without a single Southern state.
patterns.source: seed: documented technique, not yet frame-verified

patterns.label: War is declared
patterns.when: a country declares war, issues an ultimatum, mobilizes or invades

slots.message: the statement or telegram text, max 5 words

sequence: The aggressor's leader signs or reads a message at a desk or balcony.
The telegram/declaration appears as a document with a bold red phrase.
A map of the two countries; the aggressor's color flips toward the target.
Arrow and units start moving.
Crowds cheer in one place, go silent in the other.
patterns.camera: Close-up on the message, then pull out to the map.
patterns.timing: message on 'declared'; arrow on the next verb.
patterns.characters: leader + messenger; crowds on both sides
examples: Germany declared war on Russia on August 1, 1914.
patterns.source: seed: documented technique, not yet frame-verified

patterns.label: Peace is made
patterns.when: peace deal, armistice, surrender, ceasefire or a treaty between sides

slots.dove: true if peace is the point

sequence: A long table; side A on the left, side B on the right, the treaty in the middle.
Side A slumps or gloats; side B too.
The treaty's terms appear as lines on the document.
Both sign; a dove or a flag of white shows.
Crowd outside reacts.
patterns.camera: Slow push toward the document; side-to-side whip on the terms.
patterns.timing: document on its name; terms read one per clause; dove at the end.
patterns.characters: two leaders facing each other, 1-2 aides each
patterns.props: scroll or document, table, dove, flags
examples: Germany signed the armistice in a railway car in 1918.
patterns.source: seed: documented technique, not yet frame-verified

patterns.label: The scene before a battle
patterns.when: two armies meet or prepare; a named battle is introduced with its date and place
sequence: Wide battlefield with both armies on opposite sides, flags planted.
A big label: battle name + year.
Army sizes appear as counters over each side.
A commander on each side looks across; a tense line from each.
Wind/dust, silence before the charge.
patterns.camera: Slow pan across the line from one army to the other.
patterns.timing: label on the battle name; counters on the numbers.
patterns.characters: a commander + a block of 12-20 soldiers per side
examples: At dawn on June 18, 1815 two armies faced each other near Waterloo.
verified: OverSimplified 'The Napoleonic Wars' clip recorded by the channel owner (earlier session): the battle is a full-screen battlefield, not a small prop
patterns.source: verified for the full-background rule; sequence otherwise seed

patterns.label: The fighting itself
patterns.when: the fighting: charges, shelling, bombing, storming, the clash
sequence: The two blocks run at each other (enter + run actions).
Explosion and smoke at the clash point on the verb.
Close-up on the commander on the losing side reacting.
Debris, flag falls.
Camera shakes once on the biggest word.
patterns.camera: Shake on the verb; close-up on a commander on the punchline.
patterns.timing: clash on the attack verb; flag falls on the result verb.
patterns.characters: two blocks of 10-16 soldiers, a commander each
examples: The British cavalry charged straight into the French guns.
patterns.source: seed: documented technique, not yet frame-verified

patterns.label: A map explains where things are
patterns.when: borders, empires, regions, alliances: who controls what

slots.year: the year in a big counter

sequence: A dark map zooms to the region.
The relevant countries tint in their color one by one on their names.
City markers pop in on their names.
A year counter in the corner; borders change if time passes.
Zoom into the one place the next beat is about.
patterns.camera: Map view moves to fit the countries; mapzoom into the next place.
patterns.timing: each country on its name; cities on their names.
patterns.characters: none (or a small narrator char in the corner)
examples: By 1810 Napoleon controlled most of Europe.
patterns.source: seed: documented technique, not yet frame-verified

patterns.label: Something moves across the map
patterns.when: armies, ships, travelers or people move from one place to another

slots.units: hat kind or prop for the little marching figures

sequence: Map zoomed on the route.
Start city marker; the group's color flag there.
An arrow draws from start to destination, little units walk along it.
The destination marker pops on its name with a label.
Camera follows the arrow to the destination.
patterns.camera: Pan along the route, zoom to the destination at the end.
patterns.timing: arrow starts on the verb; destination marker on its name.
patterns.props: arrow with units, city markers, battle marker
examples: Napoleon marched from Paris to Moscow.
patterns.source: seed: documented technique, not yet frame-verified

patterns.label: Where are we? A city
patterns.when: the story arrives in a named city: first mention of a city as the setting

slots.detail: one prop that sums up the city

sequence: Wide painted skyline of the city with its landmarks.
Place + year banner appears.
One small action in the foreground (people walking, a cart).
Push in toward the street where the story starts.
patterns.camera: Slow pan across the skyline, then zoom 1.1 on the street.
patterns.timing: banner on the city name.
patterns.background: city with skyline key or street
examples: In Paris, the crowd was running out of bread.
patterns.source: seed: documented technique, not yet frame-verified

patterns.label: Where are we? A country
patterns.when: a country or empire is introduced as the setting, usually with a year

slots.detail: 1 sentence fact as a label (population, ruler)

sequence: Map zoom from the world to the country, the country glows.
The country's name and year appear big.
A flag or the leader's hat pops in beside it.
A fact label (population, size, ruler).
Move into the next beat's city.
patterns.camera: Zoom from wide to fit the country.
patterns.timing: country tints on its name; label +0.5 s.
patterns.characters: the country's representative char (cast kind) small in the corner
examples: In 1750 Britain was a small island with a big navy.
patterns.source: seed: documented technique, not yet frame-verified

patterns.label: A crowd reacts
patterns.when: the public reacts: cheers, boos, gasps, panic, celebration

slots.cause: what they are reacting to (a prop or a person)

sequence: The cause (a person, a news item, an event) in the corner.
The crowd faces it; all react in sync on the key word.
One individual shouts a line.
Camera cuts to the loudest person for a beat.
patterns.camera: Slow zoom into the crowd; cut to a close-up on the shouter.
patterns.timing: reaction on the key verb; shouted line 0.3 s later.
examples: The crowd went wild when the news arrived.
patterns.source: seed: documented technique, not yet frame-verified

patterns.label: A protest
patterns.when: people demonstrate, strike, boycott or demand change

slots.demand: the slogan on the main sign, max 4 words

sequence: Crowd with hand-written signs fills the street.
The main sign grows and shows the demand in big letters.
A megaphone voice; the crowd raises fists.
Opposite side: soldiers or officials stand stiff.
Standoff beat.
patterns.camera: Slow zoom on the main sign; slow pan to the opposing line.
patterns.timing: sign text on the demand word; fists on the verb.
patterns.characters: crowd 14-26, 1 leader with megaphone, opposing line of 4-8
examples: Workers marched through the streets demanding an eight hour day.
patterns.source: seed: documented technique, not yet frame-verified

patterns.label: Things get violent
patterns.when: a riot, uprising, revolt or revolution turns violent
sequence: Angry crowd with torches and pitchforks rushes in from one side.
The target building/prop catches fire on the verb.
Defenders back away or fire; smoke fills the sky.
A flag drops, another is raised.
Silence on the aftermath.
patterns.camera: Shake on the burn/storm verb; pull back to show the flames.
patterns.timing: fire on the verb; flag change +1 s.
patterns.props: fire, torches, smoke, the target building
examples: The crowd stormed the Bastille.
patterns.source: seed: documented technique, not yet frame-verified

patterns.label: A number is the story
patterns.when: a big or surprising number: money, casualties, sizes, percentages
sequence: A counter spins up to the number on the word that says it.
Icons or a bar make its size visible (one icon = a group).
A comparison appears (the size of a known city, 'twice the army of X').
A small reaction from a character.
patterns.camera: Slow zoom on the counter; hold on the comparison.
patterns.timing: counter starts on the word before the number; comparison +1 s.
patterns.background: paper or sunburst, or dark for tragic numbers
examples: The war killed more than 20 million people.
patterns.source: seed: documented technique, not yet frame-verified

patterns.label: Years go by
patterns.when: several dates or a stretch of years: a sequence over time
sequence: A horizontal line draws across the frame.
Each event pops on its date as it is spoken.
The active one grows; earlier ones dim.
A final marker at 'now' or the end year.
patterns.camera: Slow pan along the line following the narration.
patterns.timing: each event on its year word.
examples: From 1914 to 1918 Europe tore itself apart.
patterns.source: seed: documented technique, not yet frame-verified

patterns.label: A led to B
patterns.when: cause and consequence: because, led to, as a result, which meant

slots.cause: the cause as a prop or short label
slots.effect: the effect as a prop or short label
slots.link: word on the arrow (so, then, BOOM)

sequence: Left: the cause as a picture (prop or char) with a 3-word label.
An arrow draws across the middle.
Right: the effect appears, bigger or more dramatic.
A small reaction on the effect.
patterns.camera: Slow push toward the effect.
patterns.timing: cause on its word; arrow on 'so/led to'; effect on its word.
examples: The tax made the colonists angry, so they threw the tea overboard.
patterns.source: seed: documented technique, not yet frame-verified

patterns.label: Then and now
patterns.when: a change over time: how things were vs how they became

slots.left: label for before (a year or word)

sequence: The screen splits; left labeled BEFORE/year, right AFTER/year.
Left side shows the old state; a short pause.
Right side swipes in with the new state.
One character reacts differently on each side (happy vs sad).
patterns.camera: Static, then a quick push on the right side.
patterns.timing: left on the first clause; right on the second.
patterns.characters: the same character on both sides, different state
examples: London in 1800 had one million people. Fifty years later, it had two and a half.
patterns.source: seed: documented technique, not yet frame-verified

patterns.label: The economy breaks
patterns.when: a crash, depression, inflation, debt, famine or ruinous taxes
sequence: A chart or sign with the key figure falls or rockets.
A character holds an empty bag/pocket or a huge pile of worthless money.
Crowd in a line (bread line, bank queue).
One complaint bubble.
Dark vignette on tragic cases.
patterns.camera: Zoom on the chart line at the drop.
patterns.timing: chart moves on the verb; complaint 0.5 s later.
examples: Prices doubled in a year and bread cost a month's pay.
patterns.source: seed: documented technique, not yet frame-verified

patterns.label: How a machine works
patterns.when: how something works: a machine, engine, process, new weapon or factory
sequence: The machine appears large in the center.
Labels with thin arrows point to 2-3 parts as they are explained.
Something moves (gear turns, smoke rises).
The output shows (a pile of goods, a number).
The inventor/operator reacts proudly.
patterns.camera: Slow zoom on the machine; follow the labels.
patterns.timing: each label on its part word.
examples: The spinning jenny let one worker spin eight threads at once.
patterns.source: seed: documented technique, not yet frame-verified

patterns.label: Someone invents or discovers something
patterns.when: an invention, discovery, patent or breakthrough
sequence: The inventor at a workbench; a lightbulb pops above their head.
The invention is revealed with a pop and a label with its name and year.
It works (spark, movement) on the verb.
Onlookers gasp or cheer.
patterns.camera: Close-up on the lightbulb, then pull back for the reveal.
patterns.timing: lightbulb on 'idea/invented'; reveal on the thing's name.
examples: Edison tested thousands of materials before one glowed for 13 hours.
patterns.source: seed: documented technique, not yet frame-verified

patterns.label: A key figure dies
patterns.when: a death, assassination, execution or funeral of an important person
sequence: Darken the scene; the place and date appear small.
The person is shown (portrait-like), then falls or lies still. No gore.
Mourners gather; one looks up; a candle or gravestone with the years.
Slow fade.
patterns.camera: Slow zoom 1.0 to 1.1; fade to black at the end.
patterns.timing: fall on the verb; gravestone +1.2 s.
examples: Lincoln was shot at Ford's Theatre on April 14, 1865.
patterns.source: seed: documented technique, not yet frame-verified

patterns.label: People move
patterns.when: migration, settlers, refugees, colonists crossing to a new land
sequence: Map or horizon; the group with bundles walks/sails across the frame.
The vehicle carries them; the number counter ticks.
Arrival: land appears, a flag is planted or a house goes up.
A child or elder looks at the new place.
patterns.camera: Slow pan following the group.
patterns.timing: movement on the verb; counter on the number.
patterns.characters: a group of 8-14 with bundles, 1 leader
patterns.props: ship, wagon, bundles, flag, route arrow
examples: Millions of Irish families sailed to America during the famine.
patterns.source: seed: documented technique, not yet frame-verified

patterns.label: Society changes
patterns.when: rights, reform, abolition, civil rights, suffrage: a social shift
sequence: The old rule shown as a sign or barrier with a stamp.
A crowd gathers with signs.
The barrier falls or the sign is replaced on the key verb.
People celebrate (or one stands alone in somber cases).
Date label.
patterns.camera: Zoom on the sign; pull back as it changes.
patterns.timing: barrier falls on the verb.
examples: In 1920 women in the United States finally won the right to vote.
patterns.source: seed: documented technique, not yet frame-verified

patterns.label: Two people talk or argue
patterns.when: a conversation or meeting: someone said, told, asked, met, visited or shook hands with someone
sequence: Two characters face each other, the object of the talk between them.
A speaks (bubble) on the verb.
B reacts then replies.
Close-up on the one who reacts worst.
patterns.camera: Cut between the speakers' close-ups on each line.
patterns.timing: a_line on the speech verb; b_line +1.3 s.
examples: The king told his advisor he wanted more gold. The advisor said there was none.
patterns.source: seed: documented technique, not yet frame-verified

patterns.label: A secret plan
patterns.when: spies, coups, conspiracies, secret deals and sabotage
sequence: Dark room, a single lamp; plotters lean over the object.
They look around; one peeks from behind a screen.
The target is shown unaware in the next panel.
A magnifier or telegram reveals the detail.
patterns.camera: Close-up on the object; slow pull back to show the watcher.
patterns.timing: reveal on the key noun.
examples: The conspirators met in secret the night before.
patterns.source: seed: documented technique, not yet frame-verified

patterns.label: A win is celebrated
patterns.when: victory, triumph, a parade or a celebration
sequence: The winner is lifted or raises a trophy/flag.
Crowd cheers; confetti.
The loser slumps in the back corner.
Banner with the result.
patterns.camera: Slow zoom on the winner; shake on the cheer.
patterns.timing: cheer on the victory word.
examples: Britain celebrated the victory with a huge parade.
patterns.source: seed: documented technique, not yet frame-verified

patterns.label: Something goes badly wrong
patterns.when: fires, floods, plagues, sinkings, crashes, explosions
sequence: Calm before: the doomed thing appears normal.
The disaster hits on the verb (explosion, sinking, collapse).
Smoke/dark; survivors look up.
Number or date as a somber label.
patterns.camera: Hold wide; shake on the hit; slow zoom to the survivors.
patterns.timing: hit on the verb; label +1.5 s.
examples: The Titanic hit an iceberg a little before midnight.
patterns.source: seed: documented technique, not yet frame-verified

patterns.label: An ordinary story moment
patterns.when: an ordinary story beat: someone does, says or suffers something and no specific pattern above fits

slots.object: the one prop that matters (library name)
slots.label: a short on-screen label, max 28 chars

sequence: Establish the setting with the place and year.
The main character appears with a pose that matches the feeling of the line.
The one prop that matters pops in on its word.
A short label or line lands on the key word.
A second character reacts.
patterns.camera: Slow push-in; close-up on the punchline word.
patterns.timing: object on its name; line on the key verb.
examples: He kept losing at chess to a pigeon.
